In addition to the FOMC’s aggressive easing (rate to the ELB, large-scale Treasury and agency MBS purchases, expanded repo, discount window easing, elimination of reserve requirements, and coordinated dollar swap lines) aimed at stabilizing markets and supporting credit, the Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey points to a material tightening in the credit channel that will dampen transmission to the real economy. Banks reported tighter standards for C&I and CRE (including construction and land development), increased credit score thresholds, reduced credit limits, and weaker demand in several consumer categories. They also expect further tightening and reduced risk tolerance, with anticipated deterioration in loan portfolios, collateral values, and segments such as HELOCs and loans to small firms. These SLOOS signals amplify downside risks flagged in the Financial Stability Report—particularly given elevated leverage and funding fragilities—suggesting that, despite policy support, credit supply headwinds are likely to constrain activity. Net: more negative than prior given broad-based tightening and expected deterioration.
